TRUSTFORGE
A SECURE BLOCKCHAIN ECOSYSTEM FOR IDENTITY, ACCESS CONTROL & ASSET MANAGEMENT
PROBLEM OVERVIEW
  • Defence and enterprise personnel relying on centralized IAM systems risk catastrophic data leaks and single points of failure.
  • Foreign-hosted IAM platforms expose sensitive defence infrastructure to cyber espionage and unauthorized access.
  • No sovereign, tamper-proof blockchain system exists for unified identity, RBAC, and digital asset tracking.
  • Commercial IAM apps lack strict cryptographic access control, verifiable provenance, and data breach prevention.
  • Sensitive operational records and asset custody history remain vulnerable to manipulation on centralized databases.
PROBLEM SOLUTION
  • W3C-Verified DIDs – Only verified personnel, officers, and registered devices hold cryptographic self-sovereign DIDs.
  • ERC-721 Tokenized Assets – Physical and digital equipment minted as non-fungible tokens directly tied to owner DIDs.
  • Smart Contract RBAC – Role-based access control deterministically governed on-chain without central vulnerability.
  • Keccak-256 State Anchoring – All access events and credential hashes permanently locked on-chain for tamper-proof auditing.
  • On-Premise Sovereign Hosting – Fully hosted within Indian territory ensuring 100% data sovereignty under defence oversight.
  • Zero-Knowledge Attestation – Selective disclosure verifies credentials and clearances without exposing sensitive PII.

TECH STACK
FEASIBILITY AND VIABILITY
ANALYSIS OF THE FEASIBILITY OF THE IDEA
1. TECHNICAL
FEASIBILITY
Robust EVM blockchain, W3C DIDs, ZK proofs, and on-premise infrastructure are achievable using mature open-source stacks and hardened backend engines.
2. ECONOMICAL
FEASIBILITY
While initial setup requires infrastructure investment, long-term operational costs remain minimal through self-hosted EVM nodes, zero licensing fees, and microservices.
3. SOCIAL
FEASIBILITY
The platform builds deep trust among defence units and enterprise teams by guaranteeing sovereign identity ownership and tamper-proof operational record protection.
4. LEGAL & COMPLIANCE
FEASIBILITY
All data is strictly hosted within Indian sovereign territory, ensuring full compliance with CERT-In directives, DPDP Act 2023, and defence cybersecurity frameworks.
5. OPERATIONAL
FEASIBILITY
An intuitive web interface with role-based dashboards ensures frictionless onboarding, while centralized HQ-admin controls streamline lifecycle verification and audits.
6. SECURITY
FEASIBILITY
Continuous penetration testing, DevSecOps pipelines, cryptographic smart contract audits, and zero-trust perimeter defense ensure defense against state-sponsored actors.
POTENTIAL CHALLENGES AND RISKS
SECURITY VULNERABILITIES
Risk of cyberattacks from state-sponsored actors targeting smart contracts or node RPC endpoints.
USER ADOPTION & TRAINING
Personnel and enterprise operators may resist shifting from traditional legacy IAM platforms.
PERFORMANCE & SCALABILITY
Ensuring ultra-low latency transaction throughput under high concurrent load across distributed military commands.
INSIDER THREATS
Malicious administrative actions or unauthorized credential escalation from legitimate privileged users.
STRATEGIES FOR OVERCOMING THESE CHALLENGES
SECURITY HARDENING
Formal smart contract verification, automated DevSecOps pipelines, HSM keystores, and regular third-party audits.
AWARENESS & TRAINING
Zero-learning-curve UI, interactive training modules, and transparent onboarding explaining cryptographic benefits.
OPTIMIZED ARCHITECTURE
Layer-2 rollup integration, batch state commitments, Redis caching, and offline-first edge cryptographic verification.
ACCESS CONTROL & MONITORING
Enforce strict least-privilege RBAC, multi-signature admin thresholds, and tamper-proof immutable audit logging.

RESEARCH AND REFERENCES
App Interface
Web & Mobile Interface
• W3C Decentralized Identifiers (DIDs) v1.0
Summary: Defines verifiable, globally unique, cryptographically sovereign identifiers operating independent of centralized registry authorities.
Link: https://www.w3.org/TR/did-core/
• Ethereum ERC-721 Non-Fungible Token Standard
Summary: Core standard for unique, indivisible on-chain tokens utilized to represent physical equipment custody and verifiable asset provenance.
Link: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-721
• Zero-Knowledge Cryptographic Proof Systems
Summary: Mathematical verification proofs enabling selective clearance validation without revealing sensitive identities, clearances, or underlying PII.
Link: https://zkproof.org/standard/
• CERT-In Cybersecurity Guidelines for Critical Infra
Summary: Sovereign cybersecurity compliance protocols enforcing immutable audit logs, strict role boundaries, and domestic data localization.
Link: https://www.cert-in.org.in/guidelines/
